findings.text: Defines a batched asynchronous store handler with external linkage so other objects in the test build can reference it.
Defines a floating point check routine with external linkage for use by the glue translation unit.

Provides a write handler that replaces any held test firmware with an image named by caller input, issuing an asynchronous load without uevent and blocking for completion, reporting input length on success and a device error when no image arrives.

Implements a per-request worker that loads one named image either into a caller sized buffer with optional partial offset handling or through a configurable synchronous loader, recording outcome, flagging successful loads and waking its waiter before clearing its thread handle.

Offers a write handler that starts a configurable count of parallel synchronous loads in dedicated threads, refusing when a batch is already active and requiring an explicit release afterwards to widen the window where loads can coalesce.

Acts as an asynchronous batch completion callback that stores the delivered image pointer, applies a one time delay on the first slot to encourage queueing, and records a missing file outcome when the pointer is null.

Provides a write handler that launches a configurable count of asynchronous loads with caller selected uevent behaviour, marking each accepted slot and waiting for all accepted completions while propagating setup failures into the shared result.
Provides a write handler that creates a new test upload from the caller name, rejecting duplicates and allocation failures, registering with the upload core and appending to the global list.
Provides a write handler that looks up a test upload by caller name, clears any configuration selection pointing at it, then unlinks and destroys it, rejecting unknown names.
Exposes the shared numeric test outcome through a read handler delegating formatting to a shared integer helper.
Provides a write handler that releases all held firmware images and always reports the input length as handled.
Provides a read handler that copies the image selected by configuration index into the caller buffer, enforcing index bounds, presence of an active batch and image, and a single page size limit.
Provides a read handler that copies the buffer of the configured upload selection into the caller buffer, requiring a selection, successful lookup and a single page size limit.
Module initialization allocates shared configuration, initializes it, registers the misc device, and unwinds prior steps on failure with diagnostic logging.
Module teardown under lock releases held firmware, deregisters the misc device, destroys all test uploads, frees configuration and logs removal.
Performs a deterministic double precision computation exercising rounding and subnormal handling, returning success only when three derived comparisons all exceed the base value.
Wraps the floating point check with kernel FPU acquire and release, always storing one into the output slot and propagating the check status.
Registers a debug filesystem directory for selftest helpers with a read only file triggering the FPU check, refusing to load when FPU use is unavailable and removing the directory on unload.
Stress routine repeatedly allocates a high order page block, takes a speculative reference, frees the block and drops the reference, exercised under two allocation flag combinations.
A null worker argument records an invalid argument outcome in shared configuration and terminates the worker with an error.

Registered test uploads live on a global list with per entry name, buffer and handle; removal unlinks then unregisters and frees resources, and clearing all entries also clears any selected upload name in configuration.

An upload payload beginning with a textual inject marker selects a progress stage and an error name by prefix match, storing the chosen stage pointer and error code for later stage handlers to consume.

Hexdump selftest uses a fixed thirty two byte vector with an ASCII mirror and precomputed expected groupings for widths one, two, four and eight in both byte orders, honoring host endianness when selecting tables.
Expected output builder clamps rows to supported sizes, validates group size as a small power of two dividing the length, emits space separated groups then pads and appends ASCII when requested.
Two test modules prefix log output with their own module name via a format macro.
Floating point test header defines a single inclusion guard macro.
Batched synchronous start waits only for slots that launched or reported sending, leaving uninitialized slots untouched after early thread creation failure.

A single test mutex serializes custom fallback, batched start paths, upload register and unregister, firmware read paths and module teardown against concurrent attribute writes and worker completion waits.
Error names form an index addressed table keyed by the upload error enumeration, covering the full range from none through invalid image with short human readable labels.
Upload behaviour is collected in a constant operation table binding prepare, write, poll complete, cancel and cleanup slots to the test handlers.
Device attributes are exposed as a null terminated pointer array grouping reset, configuration knobs, direct triggers, batched triggers with result use, and release plus readback helpers.
Test control is surfaced as a misc device with dynamic minor assignment under the name test_firmware with associated file operations and attribute groups.

Batched synchronous loads move from idle to active upon allocation, to thread running per slot, to completed per waiter, remaining active until an explicit release clears the array; a new start while active is rejected as busy.

Batched asynchronous loads move from idle to active upon allocation, to submitted per slot, to callback completed, remaining active until explicit release; setup failure still waits for already submitted slots and overrides the shared result.

Test upload progresses through prepare validating size and arming injection, repeated writes copying bounded blocks, a poll complete check, with cancel setting a flag observed by all stages and cleanup clearing staged injection; prepare failure performs its own clearing because cleanup runs only after successful prepare.
Custom fallback frees the duplicated name immediately after submission to expose lifetime races between submitter and asynchronous completion path.
Firmware and upload readback paths reject images larger than a single page, limiting the test interface to small images.
Batched loops use an eight bit index, implicitly bounding the supported request count and risking truncation or wrap if configuration exceeds that range.
Batch callback sleeps for seconds on one slot and cancel waits poll for up to five minutes, introducing long blocking delays under test serialization or worker context.
Asynchronous batch callback treats a null image pointer as a missing file outcome because the firmware interface conveys no detailed error to callbacks.
Cancel wait bound equals five minutes expressed in milliseconds.
Hexdump test buffer totals one hundred thirty one bytes, covering thirty two triple character slots plus separators, ASCII mirror and terminator.
Selftest file is created with read only permissions for all users.
Page stress performs one million allocate reference free release cycles per flag combination using order three blocks.
